text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pilot feared dead after Swedish air force jet crashes into the Baltic Sea, narrowly missing a Russian nuclear warship en route to Kaliningrad.
- Sales of the Astra's ulcer treatment drug, Losec, rose by 37 percent in the United States in the first nine months of this year.
- Professor Bertil Hanberger is leaving his job as head of surgery at Stockholm's Karolinska hospital in protest over constant cuts in staff and funding.

- Petrol sales in Sweden fell by 1.4 percent in the first nine months of 1996 with sales, according to the Swedish Petroleum Institute. Last year about six billion litres of petrol were sold in Sweden.

- Swedish iron ore producer LKAB is down to a third of output after a three-week strike by its Norwegian workers, worried about rationalisation plans. The company says this is the worst crisis in 26 years, stopping all shipments of iron ore out of Norvik which usually ships 1.2 million ton a month.

- Swedish telephone company Telia has plans for Denmark, investing DEK 60 million in its Danish unit. The company says it may invest another billion or two if it decides to join the new cellular phone system DCS 1800.

- Swedish banks S-E-Banken and Swedbank are investing heavily in India after the Indian government's decision last week to sell 40 state-owned companies. An S-E-Banken spokesman Pedro Ekeroth says India is a very interesting market and will become a priority for his bank.
